messages:
incident-bot: Paging: error-rate spike detected for tenant=harbor-med in dedicated-pool=dp-42. Increase from 0.5% -> 18% over last 3m. Affected route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-7b-q). Severity: P1.
jen: Ack. I'm oncall. Looking at logs now.
alex: I see elevated 5xx upstream for dp-42 workers, CPU fine but tail latency rising. Possibly bad model artifact in canary.
mike: Harbor Med reported increased failed inference callbacks. Maya from CS pinged me. She's on thread. @cs_maya can you confirm customer impact?
cs_maya: Harbor Med: several live sessions saw truncation and 502s, some requests retrying causing visible timeouts for end-users. They're asking for ETA. They prefer rollback if quick.
jen: Ok — initial plan: isolate tenant traffic from canary targets, pin harbor-med to previous pinned artifact, and if needed, roll back canary. Need ops signoff for pinned-artifact deploy to dedicated pool.
sam: On call handover in 8m. Jen can you document steps so I can pickup if needed?
jen: Will do.
jen: Steps I'm going to try now: 1) Quarantine tenant traffic via routing rule -> route harbor-med to dp-42-stable (non-canary) 2) Trigger pinned artifact pinback: deploy artifact redwood-7b-q@sha256:aaaabbbb -> previous stable tag 1.13 3) Warm caches if needed.
jen: Running command to update routing config:
```bash
redwood route update --tenant harbor-med --pool dp-42-stable --sticky true --dry-run=false
```
jen: Applied route update, changes propagated to edge in ~30s. Confirming no more traffic hitting canary pods.
alex: I still see a handful of requests hitting canary nodes, probably in-flight. Starting a targeted curl to check.
jen: Triggering pinback to stable artifact now.
deploy-bot: Deployment initiated: pinback harbor-med -> redwood-7b-q:1.13 (artifact id: 7bq-1.13-202602). Job id: deploy-1856001250.
mike: Noting that dp-42 has hot KV caches pinned to the older model; warm-up might be necessary. Expect a short latency blip.
jen: Deploy completed on control plane; rolling artifacts to dp-42-stable. Verifying pod images...
jen: Pod image check: 10/12 pods rolled to 1.13, 2 still pulling.
alex: Those 2 are stuck pulling from internal registry with intermittent 503s. Kicking pull-proxy.
jen: Execing helper: 
```bash
kubectl -n dp-42 rollout restart ds/worker-model-7b-q --selector=pool=dp-42-stable
```
jen: Restart triggered, pulling resumed.
sam: Handoff: I'm oncall now, monitoring. Jen handing over.
jen: Handoff notes: pinback done, routing updated, deploy completed to stable pool, customer liaison Maya updated. Still watching for residual 5xx.
sre-lead: Good. Also ensure we've disabled autoscale burst to canary for dp-42 for next 2h to avoid accidental traffic shifts.
mike: Done: scaling policy updated to min=max=current for canary nodes.
harbor-ops-liaison: Harbor ops: we saw exactly the same pattern after daily deploy. We pinned on our side and errors dropped. Please confirm when stable for us to re-open.
cs_maya: Harbor-Med reports load normalizing slowly. They asked for a short postmortem and timeline.
alex: Logs show the canary model produced malformed tokenization for certain prompt prefix lengths — likely a bad model artifact. We'll mark artifact QC failed and block it in catalog.
jen: Marking artifact redwood-7b-q:2026-02-12 as quarantined in model catalog.
jen: Creating mitigation ticket to block future rollouts of that artifact to dedicated pools until QC fixes.
jen: Observability: error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% over 6m after pinback and routing change. Latency returning to baseline.
mike: Noting customer impact window: 1856001234 -> 1856001400 (~2.8m full impact, residual errors for next ~10m).
cs_maya: Harbor wants an ETA on when we can allow canary to proceed again. They request a full validation plan.
sre-lead: We'll do a gated rollout plan: create a short synthetic eval suite using Harbor's prompt set, run on infra canary, validate token-level diffs and regression thresholds, then canary for 1% traffic for 30m, escalate if anomalies.
jen: I'll own the validation harness + run the suite with Harbor's test prompts (Maya, please share the prompt set).
harbor-ops-liaison: Sharing prompt set in DM now.
sam: Final checks: ensure SLO alert thresholds adjusted to avoid paging on small blips during rollback, but keep a human-in-loop.
jen: Done. Adjusted alerts: threshold moved to 5% errors for 5m for dp-42, kept page on 10% for 1m.
cs_maya: Thank you — Harbor is stabilizing. They want a follow-up call in 30m and a written incident summary.
jen: I'll draft the initial incident summary and timeline, assign follow-up actions.
jen: Action items: 1) postmortem draft (jen) 2) artifact quarantine + catalog block (alex) 3) validation harness (jen) 4) customer call + summary (cs_maya) 5) review canary autoscale configs (mike).
incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, impact=tenant-isolated & pinned-artifact-rollback, responders=[jen,sam,alex,mike,cs_maya].
jen: Closing thread for now; will reopen if error rate climbs back. :white_check_mark:
cs_maya: Thanks team. Harbor appreciates the quick mitigation.
harbor-ops-liaison: We'll validate on our end and confirm when safe to reopen canary.
